transcription.text: Is it safe to work right now?
Heat says one thing. Lightning says another.
Gas says a third.
You need one place to look.
That place is Connected Environment.
One umbrella over weather, lightning, and gas.
In the portal.
Under it sit weather station, lightning, and gas.
Each with its own screens and devices.
They share one platform.
One backend. One menu and header.
The same view permission.
Projects switch on what they use.
Your site team watches and decides.
Control is narrower.
Weather limits decide when work stops.
A gas alert can be acknowledged or closed.
Recorded in WakeCap only.
Connected Products lists what each project has switched on.
Weather alone. Lightning alone.
Weather with gas.
Three projects. Three screens. One portal.
Weather showed danger.
Lightning showed all clear.
Gas showed check.
Here is the answer.
A verdict.
Danger.
With the recommended steps behind it listed in order.
A quiet station is named in the headline and marked offline.
Readiness reads not ready.
The maximum values report shows a period's peak heat index and peak wind speed across every station.
In lightning, WakeCap treats only the green state as safe to work.
Alerts are a backup.
The site's cabinet lights and sounder come first.
The gas phone page says check, then not confirmed safe.
One detector is not reporting.
The gas dashboard opens on overview.
Each card shows the worst current reading among reporting detectors.
In weather, a 30-day preview shows how often a limit would have stopped work.
Closing an alert here is recorded in WakeCap only.
The page note says it is not sent to the gas vendor.

The newest rows read Closed.
With edit access, older, acknowledged rows show a close button.
Weather stations reach WakeCap over the site's wireless mesh, through a gateway, into the cloud.
Lightning is read through a small input module, and shows on the mesh as a Modbus device.
Modbus is an industrial wiring and data standard, many sensors speak.
Gas takes another road, the vendor's cloud.
No mesh, no Modbus.
WakeCap asks that cloud on a regular timer, and each detector reports on its own schedule.
Different roads in, one platform behind them.
Weather, lightning, and gas all reach the same portal.
The platform holds readings and status from all three, a base for a future AI assistant.
Some gas history is not stored yet.
Today, building blocks exist for weather station only, not lightning or gas.
No assistant runs on any site.
An assistant could read weather readings and propose changes.
It never approves.
A person does.
People stay in control.
The weather safety answer comes from fixed rules.
An assistant would only reword it.
Your next step, open connected environment in the portal's left rail, if your project has it.
Your team stays in charge.
